title: Compass 1:1 — growth mapping scratch (Aaron & report)
content:
Purpose: quick prep for weekly 1:1 — focus on career growth mapping, next stretch opportunity, and clearing blockers. Keep it lightweight; leave time for 10–15m open check-in.

Attendees: me (Aaron) + direct report (Elena Ramos) — IC, infra team.
Context: Elena recently completed the inference cache refactor (PRs merged), took first oncall rotation last month. Expressed interest in leading a cross-team spike and moving toward tech lead responsibilities. Wants clarity on timeline for growth and concrete skills to work on.

Agenda (30m):
1) 5m - mood & wins (win: cache refactor landed; improvement in median p95 latency on dev env).
2) 10m - growth map: skills, evidence, timeline.
3) 8m - proposed stretch: lead Quantization Roadmap spike (2 sprints) + coordinate HW benchmarking.
4) 5m - action items, ask for resources, next steps.

Prep notes / signals to bring:
- Recent metrics: average PR cycle time down from 4.2 -> 3.6 days; code review backlog small but review response time spikes when oncall.
- Oncall notes: handled two incidents; did good job triaging but wants to reduce pager fatigue.
- Feedback from peer rotation: strong design writeups; could be more proactive coordinating cross-team syncs.
- Career desire: move to 'technical lead' within 6–9 months; is OK with a 3-step path if we structure milestones.

Draft growth map (talk-through with Elena):
- Month 0–2 (next 8 weeks): lead the quantization spike (design, experiment infra, result doc).
  - Evidence: spike RFC + benchmarking notebook + short demo to Platform.
  - Skills to show: cross-team coordination, experiment design, data-driven conclusions, clear tradeoff writeup.
- Month 3–5: take ownership of a small service (eg. local KV cache service) — run incident war room once, drive 1 postmortem, propose 1 reliability improvement.
- Month 6–9: mentor 1–2 juniors, run design reviews, facilitate a small roadmap decision.

Concrete stretch proposal (pitch to Elena in meeting):
- Title: "Quantization readiness spike" (2 sprints, ~6 weeks)
- Goals: evaluate 2 quantization toolchains, measure latency/cost tradeoffs on a 7B model on our Dedicated pool; produce recomendarion and a short rollout plan.
- Deliverables: experiment repo with scripts, 3 benchmark runs, cost/latency writeup, RFC draft.
- Stakeholders to loop in: Applied ML (Mina), Serving Runtime (Priya), SRE (Jon).

Notes to self (how to frame it):
- Emphasize this is a leadership opportunity: coordination + visible outcome, not just code.
- Offer blunt feedback and schedule small milestones so momentum is visible.
- Ask: how comfortable is she with stakeholder meetings? What would make those easier (templates, intro meetings, co-host)?
- Calibration: check with Priya about expected HW access windows before promising timelines.

Potential blockers and mitigation:
- Blocker: limited Dedicated GPU slots in next 2 weeks. Mitigation: arrange short benchmark window with Priya mid-sprint or use smaller batch sizes in sim env.
- Blocker: Elena's oncall rotation overlaps with spike. Mitigation: agree on protected focus blocks + shadow coverage for high-sev.

Questions to surface in 1:1:
- What part of running a cross-team spike feels most uncomfortable? (agenda: stakeholders, timeline, measurements).
- Is the 6–9 month TL timeline still motivating or too aggressive?
- What support do you want from me week-to-week? (reviews, stakeholder intros, negotiation with PMs).

Action items (clear, assignable):
- Aaron: intro email to Mina + Priya to set expectations for spike (due 2026-11-06).
- Elena: draft spike RFC outline (2–3 bullets per section) and share by 2026-11-10.
- Priya: confirm Dedicated pool availability window and recommended benchmark instance by 2026-11-08. (cc Aaron)
- Aaron + Elena: sync for 30m mid-sprint check (calendar invite) — tentatively 2026-11-20.

Follow-up notes (post-meeting template to send Elena):
- Bullet summary of agreed deliverables and timeline.
- Links to example benchmark scripts and an RFC template.
- Offer to sit in the first stakeholder kickoff to model meeting flow.

Loose thoughts / scratch (do not read verbatim):
- Could pair Elena with a senior applied ML engineer for the first week of benchmarks; reduces ramp and raises confidence.
- Consider carving a "mini feature" in the spike that delivers immediate infra value (eg. a baseline quantization inference pipeline that can be used by platform tests).
- If timeline slips because of capacity, re-baseline goals rather than kill the project — show partial results.

End.

Quick sign-off: keep tone coaching-first, concrete milestones, maintain visibility to keep momentum.
